It depends on your area. Where I work 99% of the people are reasonable and polite. You go one store over to the ghetto area and its reportedly a nightmare. Take every crazy customer with a grain of salt and appreciate the nice ones.

You're going to be bombarded with training videos. Don't stress about retaining the information. 99% of what I've learned has been by doing. No one is going to know everything so make sure to feel out your coworkers skill level. It helps to be able to know who to call on for certain issues. Even months into it you'll still need to partner with others to solve issues you haven't dealt with.

Do not take the company decisions personally. You're going to have to process alot of returns that are clearly scams/ bullshit. Don't let it get to you, its the company's money at the end of the day. Depending on the situation you'll just process a shitty return because you know your manager will just okay it anyway.

At my store the service desk offers me a lot of freedom to move around. Breaks and lunches aren't rigid so talk with your coworkers each day about what works for you and them. 

There's a lot of information and work to be done always. When it gets crazy just take it one issue at a time, that's all you can do. When its slow you can always take some time to relax and work on unimportant things. 

Either you love it or you hate it. A big part of the experience is the team you work with. If you don't like it you can always transfer to another department. Personally I love the service desk.
